description: An eight-step gate sequencer with five rows, passing its own clock signal through on the steps that are switched on, and able to jump to a random step

params.text: Sets every gate at random; held down, it re-rolls them four times a second
Sets the chance that any one gate comes out on when the gates are randomised, 0 to 1
Sets the chance, 0 to 1, that a clock pulse jumps to a random step instead of moving on to the next one
Sets how many steps the sequence runs before it wraps, 1 to 8
Switches the gate on or off for its own row at its own step

inputs.text: A rising edge moves the sequence back to the first step
A rising edge moves the sequence on one step, and this jack's voltage is what the outputs pass on
Added to the probability knob one unit per volt, with the total clamped to 0 and 1, so 1V on its own already makes every pulse jump
A rising edge sets every gate at random, using the sparseness knob

outputs.text: Carries whatever voltage is at the trigger jack while its own row's gate is on at the current step, and 0V while that gate is off

notes: the outputs copy the clock signal rather than making gates of their own, so their width and voltage are whatever clocks the trigger jack
nothing moves until a clock reaches the trigger jack
the randomise button and the randomise jack overwrite the gate buttons, so a pattern set by hand is lost
the step lamps are refreshed only on a clock pulse, so they stay as they were while the clock is stopped

inputs.0: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.1: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

continuous · one channel only

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 1V.
